title: Patchflow PR review scratchpad
content:
Quick context:
- Reviewing PR #4321 (patchflow): streaming response backpressure + KV cache split. Author: @mchen. Goal: reduce tail latency when many small streaming clients connect and while enabling partial KV-cache sharing across model variants.

High-level takeaways so far:
- Overall design is promising: separates stream backpressure control into a StreamScheduler and moves cache eviction into a background GC loop.
- Several risky coupling points: StreamScheduler currently holds a pointer to WorkerSession which then touches low-level GPU ring buffers — that leaks layers. We should push scheduling decisions to a cleaner interface.
- Tests are missing for throttling steady-state behavior (multiple concurrent clients with variable token rates). Add synthetic load tests.

Notes / Issues found (detailed):
1) StreamScheduler -> WorkerSession coupling
   - Problem: scheduler calls WorkerSession::drain_pending() directly to decide when to prefetch. That exposes ring-buffer internals and is hard to mock in unit tests.
   - Suggestion: introduce an ISchedulerClient interface with methods: current_in_flight_tokens(), push_prefetch_request(), mark_blocked(). Replace direct calls in StreamScheduler.
   - Follow-up: small refactor, low risk; can be done in a separate PR if author prefers.

2) Backpressure semantics ambiguous
   - Observed: scheduler enforces a max_tokens_in_flight (global), but no per-client minimum. If one noisy client floods, others starve.
   - Suggestion: implement weighted fairness: each client gets a token budget that decays/increases based on recent consumption. Start simple: per-client cap = min(global_cap/active_clients, burst_limit).
   - Experiment: simulate 100 clients with Poisson token arrivals; measure P99 latency and fairness index (Jain's).

3) KV cache sharing hazards
   - PR moves to shared read-only slices but also retains mutable GC list on each worker. Race possible when GC runs concurrently with a reattach of a worker to a new model variant.
   - Immediate mitigation: acquire a per-cache-version read lock during reattach; GC should attempt try_lock and defer if not available.

4) Missing observability hooks
   - Need per-request metrics: tokens_in_flight, backpressure_reason (queue_full|gpu_busy|client_slow), scheduler_decision (queued|prefetch|drop).
   - Add a lightweight event enum and emit to existing tracing/logging; ensure Console dashboards can show per-route distributions.

5) Tests and bench gaps
   - Add deterministic unit tests for Scheduler when there are N clients with staggered request times. Use deterministic clocks (fake_clock).
   - Add integration benchmark that runs on CI perf-worker: run 1h soak with synthetic clients (1k clients scaled down) and capture P50/P95/P99 and token throughput.

Checklist (what I want to see before approving / merging):
- [ ] Extract ISchedulerClient and update StreamScheduler to use it (or plan separate PR).
- [ ] Add weighted fairness algorithm + simple config knobs (per-client-burst, fairness-window-ms).
- [ ] Add read-lock on KV cache version transitions and update GC to be try-lock-friendly.
- [ ] Emit new observability events and wire to Console dashboard owners (tag: console-rollouts).
- [ ] Unit tests for scheduler determinism (fake_clock).
- [ ] Integration benchmark entry (ci/perf/patchflow) and a readme for how to run locally.
- [ ] Update PR description to include expected impact on latency/cost and mention potential tradeoffs.

Small code suggestions / snippets to save time:
- ISchedulerClient interface sketch (pseudo):
  trait ISchedulerClient {
    fn current_in_flight(&self) -> usize;
    fn push_prefetch(&self, n_tokens: usize);
    fn mark_blocked(&self, reason: &str);
  }

- Weighted fairness pseudo logic:
  per_client_budget = max( min(global_cap / active_clients, burst_limit), base_min );
  client_score += tokens_consumed * decay_factor;
  prioritize clients with lower score.

- GC try-lock pattern (rust-like):
  if let Ok(guard) = cache_version_lock.try_lock() {
    // safe to evict
  } else {
    // reschedule eviction w/ backoff
  }

Local repro / debug commands (helpful for reviewers):
- start local worker in dev mode: ./scripts/dev_worker --dev-gpu --log-level=debug
- spawn synthetic clients: ./tools/sim_client --concurrency 200 --avg-tokens 8 --burst 64 --duration 300s --endpoint localhost:8080/stream
- run unit scheduler tests: cargo test scheduler -- --test-threads=1
- perf bench locally: ./ci/bench/run_patchflow_bench.sh --clients 500 --time 600s

Performance notes observed on my runs (macbook-pro M3 dev env, not representative):
- With current PR branch: P50 ~ 60ms, P95 ~ 420ms, P99 ~ 1.3s under 200 concurrent simulated clients.
- After applying a naive per-client cap (global_cap/active_clients): P99 dropped to ~700ms, but throughput decreased by ~8% (due to extra scheduling overhead). We should attempt a hybrid where we only throttle noisy clients.

Unresolved questions (ask author):
- Is the intention for StreamScheduler to be a global process per-worker or a per-model-instance component? The PR seems mixed. Clarify design intent.
- Are there any restrictions from Dedicated customers who expect strict FIFO semantics per-connection? We need to ensure fairness knobs are off by default or opt-in per-route.

Follow-ups / small PRs I can take on (priority order):
- ISchedulerClient extraction and minimal adapter for WorkerSession (low risk). Owner: Hana (me). Estimate: 1.5d.
- Add scheduler unit tests with fake_clock + deterministic arrivals. Owner: Diego. Estimate: 2d.
- Add basic observability event enums and emit in scheduler decisions. Owner: Maya. Estimate: 1d.

Notes to self (things to mention in review comment):
- Link to perf bench results in PR description (artifact build id).
- Ask for a simple config example in repo docs to show knobs and default values.
- Recommend adding a canary rollout plan in Console for this change (route-level toggle).

Closing thought: this PR is high-value but touches racey areas. Prefer landing smaller, reviewable refactors that make behavior explicit (interfaces, locks, metrics) before the bigger GC/performance optimizations.

Raw scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Consider a hierarchical scheduler: global scheduler assigns token budgets to per-model schedulers, which then split to per-client. This allows respecting model-level SLAs while protecting workers.
- Use leaky-bucket token refill for clients with exponential backoff on sustained overuse.
- For KV caching: attach short-lived shadow refs for reattach operations so GC can see in-use refs reliably without blocking indefinitely.

End of scratchpad.
